sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a Finger.
Recognize details in shapes and objects as being similar or different from each other.
Tell a story using pictures.
Follow lines with a finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare illustrations
• Show pupils how to open their Pupil Books to the 
first page. Hold up the pupils Book so that pupils 
can see the page for lesson 1 and point to the 
first illustration.
• Say: Dooni ngolof ɗaaŋ nataal mberaan ne kom neek. ƥaaɓaan num ref neek? Iyo keek 
naakoo.
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of the bull.
• Say: Fat i ndoon qol in ɗaaŋ nataal mberaand ne. Ndax o ten fu o lakasee lengoo?" Ha'aa!!
• Point to the next picture in the row.
• Say: I ƭeetoo o lakasee. Ndax a nanda fu nataal mberaand ne? Ha' aa! 
• Point to the final picture in the row.
• Say: Ndax o heek a nanda fu nataal mberaand ne? Iyo.
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches. 

Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the Pupil 
Book.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Doon yo qol nuun ɗaaŋ nataal mberaand ne. Har o kiin ohe a fiyaa?
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what   

 the people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the   
 pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. Help   
 them see that the woman is preparing "fufu".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger 
Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Har o ƥiy o ngoor o nge nu nataal ne a fiyaa? Fat i ndimle in te fal o kupe le kam  
 poos ne! Nu pare a? Njang yo qol nuun lalit ne o kupe le retit na.
• Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger. 
• Say: Har a koyee a fiyaa? Har nu mboogu yee o ten a bugu?
• Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger. Repeat with 
the remaining image.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Recognize the front cover, and title of a book.
Apply new words learned to own life and use new words in conversation.
Use background knowledge to build meaning.
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, 
back, Title
• Point to the cover and back of a book.
• Say: Han i  niir ngotit njasnoor mbaam a cinj. 
• Keek refu njasnoor ne na laf a peraandee nu 
safe jangir le. Xa ñuxur ake ndefna nu begir safe 
jangir naa lalaa in xa ñuxur ake i mbarna yo o 
niir
• Say: : I mbadangaa me a nax ale fagit na, han i nga' a cinjee nu safe jangir le.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils 

what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.. 
  cigeenes, camnum, o nged

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments   
 such as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned. 

      Faatu Fa Neewu 

 Faatu sawar'ee.
Ahe ref a nu mbindaa too ref'ee fiyaa dara. 
Te ga' a faaptewum Ami te unaa fufu.
Te layee, "Faaptew, ndax waagaaxoŋ o dimle?"
Te layinee, "Hee ha aa, Faatu, ke o jangaa a maya lool!" 
Koy te ret a ƭatum.
Te ga'o maasirum te leemaa a pañe'mee cagu.
Te layinee, "O cigeenes, ndax waagaaxoŋ o dimle"? 
"Hee, ha aa, Faatu, ke o jangaa a maya lool!"
Koy te ret a ƭatum.
Koy, te ga'o caminum te xooxaa no nged.
Te layinee, "O camines, ndax waagaaxoŋ o dimle"?
Te layinee, "Hee, ha aa, Faatu, ke o jangaa a maya lool!" 
Koy, te ret a ƭatum.
Koy, te ga'o cigeenum te fiyaa calel o jangandum. 
Te layinee, "O cigeenes, ndax waagaaxoŋ o dimle"?
Te layee, "Hee, ha aa, Faatu, ke o jangaa a maya lool!" 
A paam o ndik, te ret maana faapum.
Faapum a layinee, "Faatu es, har taxu o fuux?"
"Kaan jangaa mayu in naangaa unaa fufu. 
Kaan jangaa mayu in naangaa jagandaa a pañe. Kaan jangaa mayu in naangaa xooxaa no 
nged. Kaan jangaa mayu in naangaa fiyaa calel o jangand. Har waagum o'fi?"
Faapum a layinee, "Hee Faatu! Bar o fuux! Maakof ne a doya. Bugaamii o haa waagaxama 
o dimle bon leem xa soraas ake na pañe ke. Ndax han o dimle'aam?" Koy te dimle in.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading from. 
Ask what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")

• Say: Tam waago ga' o no'tandee na naxee? (correct response: (begir njasnoor).
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer. Call on a second volunteer pupil to say the title of the 
story that was just read aloud.
• Say:  I mbadangaa me safe jangir le fodna, har i nga' kaa? (correct response: (begir ne a 
cinjee)
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes, and with a finger.
Recognize details in letter shapes as being similar or different from each other
Follow lines with their finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters 
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see 
the page and point to the first capital letter. 
Do not say the name of the letter - this is 
NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It 
is an activity for pupils to practice telling the 
difference between letter and shapes.
• Say:  Mexe jangaa qoles joox no o hiiƈ o 
feraandee. Bar o leng a jooxit ngolum. Han i 
mbaaƭ o lakasaa nand na fo o ten. 
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: Fat i ndoon qol in took o hiiƈ o feraandee. Ndax den fo feraandee a nanda yo? Ha'aa!
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: I mbaaga ƭeeƭ o lakasee. Ndax den fo feraandee a nanda yo?
• Point to the final one in the row.
• Say: Ndax den fo feraandee a nanda yo? Iyo.
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it. 

Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page of the  
 Pupil Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn   
 letters. It is an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. Ask 
pupils to point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct answer)

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Say: I ndeefoo xa tiqañoow a keek! O feraandee ndambasoƈoo! I ndoon qol in me i ndopit 
na koy i ndeefoo nete foolit na na lafee.
• Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
• Repeat with the remaining images.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Know that words are separated by spaces.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Answer factual questions.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately

activities.title: Words are separated by spaces
activities.content:
Describe what a word is, and why there are 
spaces between them
• Take out the read aloud book from yesterday's 
lesson. Choose a sentence to write on the board.  
• Say: Ɗelem leek xatu na naxee niiran'uuma a nuun. Han i njoktoor nu teendeer ke ndefna 
xa ñuxur ake nu ɗelem. In niira ngaa, han niir xa ñuxur ake o leng o leng, yaam o ñuxur 
nuu refna a jega kaa te firit na.
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: Teendeer ke ndefna na xa ñuxur ake naa lalaxam a palaas no ñuxur fo me o ñuxur o 
lakasee ropitna.
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Say: Teendeer ke na xa ñuxur ake naa ndamit kaa yo a nuun bo nu mbaag o niir. Mbanuu 
o mbindaa a ƭelem a pogreer, teendeer ke ndefna a ndeer xa ñuxur ake naa ndamit kaa 
nuun.
• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new sentence.
• Say: Doon yo qol nuun ɗaaŋ o ñuxuree. Ndiiki, lalyaamo o ñuxur o lakasee. Nam i lalit kaa 
nguutatir ne refna a ndeer xa ñuxur xa ƭak ake. (A jega teendeer a ndeer den).
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two  
 words, and put their fingers on it.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.
Recognize sight words.
Read sentences using sight words and pictures.
Draw simple shapes.

activities.title: Read sight words
activities.content:
Learn two new sight words
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in the 
Pupil Book.
• Say: O heek Moodu yoo. O heek Faatu yoo. Han I 
niir tig mayu na den nu hap neek.
• Say: Ndoon yo qol nuun ɗaaŋ o ñuxur [Moodu] ɗaaŋ nataal ne no ƥiy o ngoor o nge.   
 Ndoon yo qol nuun ɗaaŋ o ñuxur [Faatu] ɗaaŋ nataal ne no ƥiy o ndew o nge.
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to [Moodou] on the left side, then point to the matching name on the  
  right side. Repeat with [[Faatu].
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching name in the  
 row.
· Continue in the same way with each row.

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say:  Ga' aam a [Faatu] took o laf o leek. Ndiiki ga' aam o ñuxur o xas! O ñuxur o xaseek 
• refu [ɗeet]. Yaam I anda [Faatu] fo o ñuxur o xaseek, I mbaaga niir har nataal keek layaa. 
• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to name the 
picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the pictures/
word with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.
• Point to pictures or words as you read. [Moodu ga'a famb]. 
• Remind pupils that "ga'a" means "to observe" or "to see." 
• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture sentence 
again together.

• Say: Ndiiki, an ga'o a langee? Fat i ndoon qol in took ɗelem le koy niirandoor ɗelem le 
[Faatu ga' a taabulee].
• Say: An waagu niir ɗelem le reefna?
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects  
Point to the next activity in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Fat i ndoon qol in ɗaaŋ nataal mberaand ne. Har nu nga'u? Ndax nu nga'a dumbul le 
reefuuna?
• Point to the next picture in the row.
• Say: Iyo, naakoo! Naak le fo mbaal ne har a nguutatiru yo?
• Continue with other illustrations.

activities.title: Draw shapes
activities.content:
Practice drawing common shapes
• Ask pupils to trace each shape in the Pupil Book with one finger.
• Ask pupils to try to draw 3 of each shape in their exercise books. Depending on their   
 comfort with writing and drawing, different pupils may focus on just one shape or draw   
 many.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes and with a finger
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger
• Say: In naangaa o niiraa, naangaam o ɗeetaa 
xa ñuxur ake o leng o leng. O ñuxur nuu refna a 
jega kaa te firit na. Pur o and ke o niiraa, a jega 
o njiriñ pur o niir o ñuxur nuu refna. O doonaa 
ngolof ɗaaŋ o ñuxur nuu refna, hana damitoŋ bo 
fool kiro xa ñuxur o naangaa niiraa
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate 
how to track with your finger under each word as 
you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger 
under the specific word.

• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while you 
read it aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils 
what they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know. 
 feedeejam         saŋke         doktoor

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud
• use the appropriate big book or  supplementary illustrations if available
• Part way through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your 
finger below each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make a big 
sweeping motion back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking with your 
finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud. 

    Aadama fa Ndeɓ a Kaa te Sibitu (Maleeriya)
Aadama fa ndeɓ ahe gena fa yaayum fa faapum.
Yaayum fa faapum, a ngooyin, a layinoo yee, "Aadama! A ndokee ahe yunga. Naneeroo o leng 
a jaaɓ. Taa Aadama?
Aadama a nana yaayum a hooyan. Aadama a nana faapum a hooyan. Aadama jaaɓee. Te a 
burle a wondoox nu njoŋ ne. Yaay fee fa faap fee a ƭeetiroo. Yaay fee ƴuf na ndok Aadama.
Yaay fee layee, "Aadama, feedeejam. Naa fiyo?" Aadama doonin, "Hee yaa. Kaan jir!" 
Yaayum a doon o ɓayum na tagidum, te layee, "O ɓaalfee a sumayii lool! Han hooy a doktoor 
fee! Faapum a hooy a doktoor fee no mobaayilee.
Doktoor fee a gar a ɗeet a Aadama koy a layee, "O ɓaalfee a suma lool! I mbaadinoo jirof le!" 
O fudee na Aadama a ɗomaa, ndiiki te layee, doktoor doktoor! ndax kaan xon kaa?" Doktoor 
fee a jal a layee, "Ha aa, Aadama! Han cooɗoŋ teex koy o ɗaan!"
Yaayum a lay a doktoor fee yee "Jookanjal! Doktoor fee layee, "Barnu mbeec teex ke. Daltin 
haye faam a paam, Aadama a warayii ɗaan ɗaaŋ saŋke ngooƴe nu teex.
Yaayum a ɗeet a faapum a layee, "Fat I njik saŋke haye! Heɗaaxoŋ, ƴufi a paax ret nu marse 
faa!" Aadama nan ke de layaa koy te wondoox.
Keek a nanta a nax nu ngoor teɓ ne maleeriya a moytooxteel fo ne te waadiniteel, saƭikinaa o 
njiriñ a baadin fu wondooxaa ɗaaŋ saŋke ngoƴe fu teex.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their 
own words.
• Say: Ndiiki i mbaaga njang xa ñuxur ake i njang na yo pur i njagand a ƭelem.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in 
a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct 
the pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't skip words 
while reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or follow under the 
words with your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

random to read the first sentence. Ask another pupil to read the second, then continue for 
each of the sentences. Ensure that pupils know the correct way to read each sentence.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who" ("An")
• Read the question: 
• Say: An hooy u a doktoor fee ye Aadama a jir iina? Answer: (Faap Aadama hooy u doktoor 
fee ye Aadama jir iina).  
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "an" is asking about. Call on 
one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. 
(Response: the question word "an" asks us the name of a someone or something alive)
• Teach pupils to use the question word ("tam")
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "tam." Tell pupils that they 
will use it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: 
• Say: O jirangaa tam naango o retaa?
• Say: O ñuxuree 'tam' naa layaa in o doonooɗ , a palaas mbaa tig. 
• Read the question:
• Say: Tam Aadama ref u ye yaayum fa faapum a ngooyeeguuna? Answer: (Aadama ahe 
• ref a kam a ndokum ye yaayum fa faapum a ngooyeeguuna).
• Say: I ngelaat a palaasee i niir iina. A naxee a laya yee: Bo ndiiki ahe wondooxa nu njoŋ 
ne.
• Ask pupils to think about "where", or the place, that this happened. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Tam faap Aadama a jiktu saŋke ne? Answer: Faap Aadama ahe jikta 
saŋke ne nu marse faa.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to 
the question. Remind pupils that it is a "tam" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Evaluate pupils use of the keyword "where" ("tam")
• Say: Question Introduction: What word can we identify that asks about a place or 
situation in a story? 
• Say: O ñuxur o lum  i mbaagu anditee a palaas mbaa xew xew naa laamiteel kam a nax?
• Call on a pupil at random who raised their hand. Remind them that the word is "where" 
(tam)

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book, spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
• Know what the "cover " and "back " of the 
book means.
• Understand that words in print are separated 
by spaces. 
• Know that tracking a finger under a word helps 
keep track of where you are reading.

1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means.
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and explain. Give 
more examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure to support them in 
this skill during the next lessons.
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "back" of the book. Give feedback, and   
 explain and give more examples if needed. 

2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture for the 
story, so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read this story yet, 
but that is alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put their 
finger on that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give 
feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: : Teendeer ke naa laltaa yee xa ñuxur xa ƭaq a keek a nguutatir a yii. 

3.  Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are reading
• Open a big book (any big book) to the first page. Ask pupils to watch and listen. Read the 
first sentence while pointing to (tracking) each word with your finger.

• Ask pupils what you were doing with your finger. Then ask them why you did that. Tell the 
pupil who responds if they are correct or not. Then repeat or say the correct response.

Teach the Letter

poster or on the board.

• Point to the lower case letter "a" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ke moƴna may, han i ga'in te binteel neek na xa ñuxur.

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap two-syllable words
• Say: Nu mbaaga ngaaj o ñuxur na xa qiɓ. O hiɓ nuu refna hana jeg o nanel o hiiƈ rew, kom 
ne i njangit uuna. (a ba). 
• Model by clapping:  →  a/ba /
• Practice together with pupils:  Aba→ /a ba/, Aba→a ba
• Pupils practice alone: daba→/da ba /, Daba→/Da ba/
• Clap words with different numbers of syllables
• Say: Ha ñuxur xa keek a njega xa qiɓ a ƭak, ndaa o ñuxur a waaga jeg o hiɓ o leng, xa qiɓ 
xa tadaq, mbaa kaa hupna. Fat i njeemoo xa ñuxur o ndik koy i ƭeet. Han lay o ñuxur o 
feraandee. Ndiiki, fat i mboxandoorin a caf a ƭak. 
• Words: INSERT 2 and 3 syllable words with the new vowel  
 (mama: ma/ ma, satala: sa/ta/la, almet: al/met, arka: ar/ka, fafadi: fa/fa/di)

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Har nu ga' u?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help   
 pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Fat I mboxandoor xa qiɓ ake no ñuxuree (aba). A caf a ponum nu nanu o   
 nanelee /a/ no ñuxuree (aba)? I ƥaat o mbox.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the  
 sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or another   
 language they know.
• Say: I layandoor o ñuxur o lakasee (daba). Ndax nu nana o nanel o hiiƈ rew /a/ kam o   
 ñuxuree (daba)? A jaf a ponum nu nanun?
• Say: Ndiiki, koy nuuno yoo. Lay yo o ñuxuree. Nu naangaan o layaa, ndoon yo qol nuun   
 ɗaaŋ o hiiƈee /a/ nu laya ngaa nanel ne /a/. 

Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Fat o huu refna doon ngol ɗaaŋ nataal ne no'eena "arka" na langee.
• Say: Har nu nga u? O ten refu "arka".
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: O nanelee /a/ tam a waage o qic. Ten refu I naangaa  layaa, I qic o nanelee pur te 
jigid. Ndax nu nana o nanel o hiiƈ o rew o jiigee /aa/ no ñuxuree (mbaal).
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the 
same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to 
each other. Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two /a/ together, it makes a long sound /aa/. The long 
sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the 
syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
• Read the following story aloud (use the appropriate big book or supplementary    
 illustrations if available)
• During reading, stop to discuss people and places
• Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the   
 pictures, where they think the story takes place. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, what  
 the characters like to do. Assure pupil responses are related to the pictures.

• Where do you think they are? How do you know? What more can you say about that   
 place?
• Who do you think this person is? What is he/she doing?

      Isaa fu Jaajalum 
Meen a reeɗu, reeɗ, Isaa gen a yii no qol.
Kom leng, te ga' ee a buga yii wiin waa naa njalanan no qolum. Te ret nu max ne koy te heɗin, 
a layinee"O feet, o gar jalanaam."
Max ne layinee, "A ref a ngaa a cek garkee, han gar." Isaa layinee, "Ha'aa, a cek garkee."
Isaa ret mena cekee koy te layinee, "O feet, o gar jalanaam."
A cekee layinee, "A ref a ngaa han a maf a gar, garkiim." Isaa layee, "Hee ha'aa! A maf 
garkee."
Isaa a ret mena mafee koy te layinee, "O feet, o gar jalanaam."
A mafee a layee, "A refa ngaa o ɗana hana gar, garkiim." Isaa layee, "Hee ha'aa, o ɗana 
garkee"
Isaa a ret men o ɗana he koy te layinee, "O feet, o gar jalanaam." O ɗana he layee, 
"A refa ngaa fangool hana gar, garkiim." Isaa layee, "Hee ha'aa, fangool garkee".
Isaa ret na fangool fee koy te layinee, "O feet,o gar jalanaam."
Fangool a layinee, "A refa ngaa han o loq a gar, garkiim." Isaa layee, "Hee ha'aa, o loq 
garkee."
Isaa ret no loqee koy te layinee, "O feet, o gar jalanaam."
O loqee layinee, "A refa ngaa han fiɗel a gar, garkiim." Isaa layee, "Hee ha'aa, fiɗel garkee." 
Isaa ret no fiɗel koy te layinee, "O feet, o gar jalanaam."
Fiɗel layinee, "A refa ngaa han a teƥ a gar, garkiim." Isaa layee, "Hee ha'aa, a teƥ garkee."
Nu nges naa, deno fop a ndetoo no qol Isaa. 
A cekee a gis max ne.
A mafee a raxin a cekee fo xa ñeekum. 
O ɗana he a room a mafee.
Fangool fee a ŋat o ɗana he. 
O loqee a war a fangool fee. 
Fiɗel fee a dox o loqee.
A teƥee a ñuf fiɗel fee. 
Koy Isaa ƴuf a ret.

• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on   
 one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why.

Teach pupils to use the question word "when" ("mban")

 will use it to answer the next question.

 school, on the weekend)

activities.title: Letter and keyword

Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "i" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say:  Keek ref o hiiƈee o xasee pur kom ne haye. O hiiƈeek o ten ref o nanel /i/. I 
lanyandoor: /i/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "I" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Keek o hiiƈ o leengee yoo. O ten tamit naa cooxtaa o nanel /i/. Mbanuu te ropna 
• ɗelem mbaa gon, han i nga'in te binteel neek.
• Point to the small letter "i" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ke moƴna may, han i nga'in te binteel neek na xa ñuxur.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.

• Say: Har nu nga'u?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help 
pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: I mboxandoor xa ƥay in te yoon fu hiɓ le. A caf a ponum nu nanu /i/ no ñuxuree 
"gin"? I ƥaato mbox.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the 
sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another 
language they know.
• Say: I layandoor o ñuxur o lakasee. O ñuxur o lakasee ten refu "ndoki". Ndax nu nana o 
nanel o hiiƈ rew /i/ kam o ñuxuree "ndoki"? A caf a ponum nu nanun?
• Say: Ndiiki, koy nuuno yoo. Lay yo o ñuxuree. Nu naangaan layaa, ndoon yo qol nuun ɗaaŋ 
o hiiƈee /i/ nu laya ngaa o nanelee /i/.
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say:  Fat o huu refna doon ngol ɗaaŋ nataal mberaand ne a langee? Har nu nga'u? O ten 
refu "ŋoosi".
Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: O nanelee /i/ tam a waage o qic. Ten refu i naangaan layaa, i qic o nanelee pur te 
jigid. Ndax nu nana o nanel o hiiƈ o rew o jiigee /ii/ no ñuxuree (ñiig)?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the 
same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to 
each other. (Answer: two)
• Tell pupils that when they see two "i" together, it makes a long sound /ii/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.

syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

Kombe fu Fambe le
Kombe fu ƥasilum ngen u. Awe njeg a yo a tuul a ƭak, a cek a tadak, naak, fu fambe. Fambe 
le jegee fayda. Tusuur, a naanga yii jalnooraa a Kombe fu ƭapatum ne.
Kom leng, Kombe a ga'a yii fambe le te fiyaa kaa faaxeerna. Te ƴuf a lay kin a yaayum. 
Ndaa, yaayum ahe refa jalaa. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa." Te ƴuf maana 
faapum. Ndaa, faapum tamit ahe refa jaleega. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa." 
Te ƴuf a lay kin o maagum o koor. Ndaa, o maagum o koor tamit ahe ref a jalaa. Te layee, 
"Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa." Te ƴuf a lay kin o maagum o tew. Ndaa, o maagum o tew 
tamit ahe ref a jalaa. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa."
Palakaan ke, te ƴuf a lay kin a maamum fa ndew. Maamum fa ndew ref ee fiyaa dara. Te 
layinee, "Kombe, gari lalaam o ten." Den fop de ƴufandoor a ƭeet koo fambe le. Fambe le 
a ƴaqeega toki. Maam fa ndew fee a wuuq, a layee "Hee Roog o yaal in! "Fambe le ahe 
ƴaqaa toki es ke! Yaay fee a ƴufiidaa a wuuqaa, a layaa yee taa xa ñafaƭes? Faap fee a 
ƴufiidaa a wuuqaa,a layaa yee, taa
ngembes? O maagum o koor a ƴufii daa a wuuqaa, a layaa yee, taa darapes? O maagum o 
tew a ƴufii daa a wuuqaa, a layaa yee, taa ilifoŋes ne?
Deno fop a ƭeet fambe le. Fambe le a ƭeet a den koy a lool. Maam fa ndew fee a yoɗ toki um 
ke koy te ling a Kombe. Te layee, "Jookanjal ye layaxamoona ke fambe le a fiyee giina."

them to find the matching vowels by themselves.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud

to ask them what they remember from yesterday's reading. 
Kombe fu Fambe le
Kombe fu ƥasilum ngen u. Awe njeg a yo a tuul a ƭak, a cek a tadak, naak, fu fambe. Fambe le 
jegee fayda. Tusuur, a naanga yii jalnooraa a Kombe fu ƭapatum ne.
Kom leng, Kombe a ga'a yii fambe le te fiyaa kaa faaxeerna. Te ƴuf a lay kin a yaayum. Ndaa, 
yaayum ahe refa jalaa. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa." Te ƴuf maana faapum. 
Ndaa, faapum tamit ahe refa jaleega. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa." Te ƴuf a lay 
kin o maagum o koor. Ndaa, o maagum o koor tamit ahe ref a jalaa. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, 
waasi ke o sosaa." Te ƴuf a lay kin o maagum o tew. Ndaa, o maagum o tew tamit ahe ref a 
jalaa. Te layee, "Hee Kombe, waasi ke o sosaa."
Palakaan ke, te ƴuf a lay kin a maamum fa ndew. Maamum fa ndew ref ee fiyaa dara. Te 
layinee, "Kombe, gari lalaam o ten." Den fop de ƴufandoor a ƭeet koo fambe le. Fambe le a 
ƴaqeega toki. Maam fa ndew fee a wuuq, a layee "Hee Roog o yaal in! "Fambe le ahe ƴaqaa 
toki es ke! Yaay fee a ƴufiidaa a wuuqaa, a layaa yee taa xa ñafaƭes? Faap fee a ƴufiidaa a 
wuuqaa,a layaa yee, taa
ngembes? O maagum o koor a ƴufii daa a wuuqaa, a layaa yee, taa darapes? O maagum o tew 
a ƴufii daa a wuuqaa, a layaa yee, taa ilifoŋes ne?
Deno fop a ƭeet fambe le. Fambe le a ƭeet a den koy a lool. Maam fa ndew fee a yoɗ toki um ke 
koy te ling a Kombe. Te layee, "Jookanjal ye layaxamoona ke fambe le a fiyee giina."

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Where" ("Tam")
• Read the first question: Tam fambe le a fi'teegu ɗofaanax? Answer: Fambe le ahe fi'teega 
ɗofaanax kam a ndokee.
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on 
one or two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. 
(Response: the question word "where" asks us about a place)
Teach pupils to use the question word "what" ("Har")
• Read the question: 
• O ɓiy ndaxar num moƴo bug?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer.
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "what." Tell pupils that they 
will use it to answer the next question.
• Say: O ñuxuree "har" a nangee laamtiteel tig mbaa o ngelaat o doonooɗ. I nanangaa 
"har", han i andee o doonooƭee han a ref tigaa waagoona o ga' mbaa o duqin.
• Say: Nu ga'angaa ƥaaɓaan naa museeruuma o ga' koy in laamit, "Keek haroo?" Bugaamii o 

and gon le nu ƥaaɓaan ne. In laamitangaa, "har?" bugaamii o and tig nu ke a kangaamee  
fi'na.
• Read the question: Har yaay Kombe a fiyaa? Answer: Yaay Kombe a uneega yii fufu.
• Say: Fat i ngeelaatoo ke i niir iina yo. A naxee a layee: 'Yaayum a jaleegayii ndax a uneega 
yii fufu.
• Ask pupils to think about what, or the thing, they are asking about. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Har fambe le ƴax u? Answer: Famble a ƴax a yii toki.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. Remind pupils that it is a "what" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

ɗelem mbaa gon, han i nga'in te binteel neek.
• Say: Ke moyna may, han i nga'in kom neek na xa ñuxur.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: Har nu nga'u?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help 
pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Fat i mboxandoor a qiɓ ake no ñuxuree. A caf a ponum nano o nanelee /o/ no ñuxuree 
"ndol"? I ƥaat o mboxan a qiɓ ake.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the 
sound, help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another 
language they know.

• Say:  I layandoor o ñuxur o lakasee: 'oto'. Ndax nu nana o nanel /o/ kam o ñuxuree 'oto'? 
A caf a ponum nu nanun?
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Fat o huu refna a doon ngol ɗaaŋ nataal mberaan ne. Har nu nga'u? O ten refu 
"rato".
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: O nanelee /o/ a waaga ref o nanel o jiig. Ten refu i naangaan o layaa, i qic o nanelee 
pur te moƴ o jigid. Ndax nu nana o nanel /oo/ o jigidu le kam o ñuxuree "xoox".
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the 
same vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to 
each other. Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two "o" together, it makes a long sound /oo/. The long 
sound means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long 
(stretched) sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the   
 syllables and listen for the long vowel in the word.

activities.content:

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story

pupils. 
Say: Faap fo o ƥeem awe ŋaaya o faam. I niir pur and na den. 
• Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they 
should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit 
with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list.
• Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may 

indicate that the child is struggling. 
• Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
• Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning 
of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your 
pupils found challenging in the assessment. The 
skill reinforced by the activity is in the activity 
name: "letter sounds" or "syllable blending".

Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have 
already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to 
participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say 
its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). 
Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. 
When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class 
has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give 
a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. 
Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote 
down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation 
from the class.

• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the 
picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the 
list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the 
class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.

the board.
• Say: O ñuxuree refu "baaba". Ndiiki, i mbinda yo o ñuxuree fop. I niirandoorin.  
(Pupils read the word)

syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with

Words: beebe: bee/be/ boobo: /boo/bo/
Use syllables to build new words

• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they 
know and write it in their copy books.

Faatu Fo O Ngoolo Nge
Faatu o ndoog o ndeɓ o sawaru yoo.
A naanga ŋasaa fu ƥaaɓaan mayu, a taaƭ, a ƥil, ngoor tew, fu kuu te waag na o jeg kam a

Ndaa ke te moƴ'iina bug o ŋasit ten refu o ngool o nge.
Mbanuu refna a bugeega yii o daaw o ngool o nge ndaa waag i ran.
Te ŋaay took ndaxar njiig a foogee o ɓaymee hana daaw o ngool o nge, ndaa daawiran. Te diƴ 
a siwo foofi koƭu koy a ƭeetaa leer ne no ngool o nge.
Te a rok kam a ndokum, ndaa te ga'ee o ngool o nge a muda!
Te ƭeet nu ɗeendooree, koy te ga' o ngool o lakas! Ndaa a anda yee o ngool o lengoo.
Ye o ngool o nge a feeñ na, a bet aanii.
Te fod took njongum a lool bo faapum a nanin. Faapum a gar kam a ndokee.
Faapum a laamitinee, "Faatu es, har taxu o loolaa?" 
Te dooninee, "Waagiim o dam o ngool o nge!"
Faapum a layinee, "Moskiro waag o dam o ngool o nge. Ke waagoona o fi' o ten refu o dam 
leerum."
Faatu foogee a jega leer mayu, kaa ngoor mayu a mbaag na o ŋasit. Ndaa o ngool o nge o 
lengoo, o haa o leng a waageerna o dam.
Te layee, "Kaaga a faaxa. O ten refu yee o ngool o nge fop njegun.".

Faatu Fo o Ngool o Nge
Faatu o ndoog o ndeɓ o sawaru yoo.
A naanga ŋasaa fu ƥaaɓaan mayu, a taaƭ, a ƥil, ngoor tew, fu kuu te waag na o jeg kam a

diƴa siwo foofi koƭu koy a ƭeetaa leer ne no ngool o nge.

Te fod took njongum a lool bo faapum a nanin. Faapum a gar kam a ndokee.
Faapum a laamitinee, "Faatu es, har taxu o loolaa?" Te dooninee, "Waagiim o dam o ngool o 
nge!"
Faapum a layinee, "Moskiro waag o dam o ngool o nge. Ke waagoona o fi' o ten refu o dam 
leerum."
Faatu foogee a jega leer mayu, kaa ngoor mayu a mbaag na o ŋasit. Ndaa o ngool o nge o 
lengoo, o haa o leng a waageerna o dam.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils found 
challenging in the assessment. The skill reinforced by the 
activity is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or "syllable 
blending "
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.

Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly.

Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs.

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

Fangool Fa Ndeɓ Fee
Kom leng, fangool fa ndeb a sutoox a yii kam a saxal a teɓ. Te ɗeet ke wirlooxuuna koy te ga' 
o riiƭ.
ndiiƭ ne lay a fangool fa ndeɓ fee yee, "Wo de jegiro o nand." Fangool fa ndeɓ laamitinee,

Ndiiƭ ne layinee, "Yaam jegiro a kand." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a fuux koy te a ret.
Miñee sax te het fa a ƭeem.
A ƭeemee layinee, "Wo de jigiro o nand." Fangool fa ndeɓ laamitinee, "Har taxu?" A ƭeemee 
layinee, "Yaam waagiro a yet."
Fangool fa ndeɓ a moƴo retaa rek a het fu faaɓ. Faaɓ le layinee, "Wo de jigiro o nand."
Fangool fa ndeɓ laamitinee, "Har taxu?"
Faaɓ le layinee, "Yaam jegiro a caf too waagiro a pool."
Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a lool, Te layee,"Hee Ha'aa! Ndigil ndigil a waagarefee jigiim o nand."
Koy fangool fa ndeɓ fee a het fa a maf. A mafee laamitinee, "Wo ref an?" Fangool fa ndeɓ fee 
a layinee, "Andiim."
A mafee a layinee, "Reti haad o waaƭ ka yaayof." Koy fangool fa ndeɓ fee a sakitoox.
Te ga' fangool fa njiig, fa ƥalgu faa naa meleƴaa. Yaay fee na fangool fee layinee, "O ƥees! 
Tam ret o?"
Fangool fa ndeɓ fee muuƴoox. Ndiiki andaam:
Ndeke a jegaam o nand.
Fangool ref'um----too kaaga doya.

ake: /de/ /di/ /do/.

each sound, and then the syllable.

the syllables independently again from their books.

Fangool Fa Ndeɓ
Meen a reeɗ u reeɗ, gin deɓ reeɗ o meen. Te wondoox u a lang kam daaƭ le. Kom leng, gin le 
woƴtoox koy fangool fa ndeɓ a sutoox. Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a woot a yee. Te ɗeet ke
wirlooxoona fop, koy te ɗeet took, a ga' o riiƭ o deɓ. O riiƭ o deɓee a layee, "Hee! fangool fa 
ndeɓ fee, "wo jegiro o nand." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee laamitinee, "Har ref na mi kaa jegeer na o 
nand." O riiƭ o deɓee a layee, "Jegiro a kand mbaa a naf." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a layee, "Har 
warum o fi'nu kaaga? Ndiiƭ ne a layee, "Waagaa o ret o laamit o fiɗee."
Te ga o fiɗ o mosu o laa doŋ na took ndaxar. O fiɗee lay a fangool fa ndeb fee yee, "Wo 
jegiro o nand." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a lamitinee, "Har ref na mi kaa jegeer na o nand." O fiɗee 
layee, "Jegiro a kand too wagiro a yet." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a laamitinee, "Har warum o 
fi'nu kaaga?" Te layinee, "Waaga o ret laamit a faaɓ." Koy fangool fa ndeɓ fee a ɓood a ret a 
waaƭik faaɓ le.
Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a fad no o quluɓ. Te ga faaɓ deɓ a moof took ɓil. Faaɓ deɓ a ɗeetin a 
layee, "Hee fangool fa ndeɓ fee, "Wo jegiro o nand." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a laamitinee, "Har 
ref na mi kaa jegeer na o nand." Faaɓ deɓ a layee, "Wo jegiro a caf too waagiro o weƴ nen 
weƴtaa." Fangool fa ndeɓ fee a layee, "Har warum o fi koy? Nu waxtu faaga rek, Moodu 
fadiid no quluɓee. Te ɗeet fangool fa ndeɓ fee koy te laamitinee "Wo refu an?" Fangool fa 
ndeɓ fee a dooninee, "Mi de andiim! Ke anduuma o ten refu yee mi jegiim o nand." Moodu 
layee, "Hee ha'aa! Heɗaaxoŋ, ɓoodi o sakitoox nu mbin nuun o waaƭik a yaayof." Koy fangool 
fa ndeɓ fee a ɓood a sakitoox maan gin laa te woƴtooxit iina.
Ye te fad na ma, te ga' ƥaaɓaan naa te moseer o ga'. A jigid a yii a ɓodax, a jeg a piis a ƥaal 
fa tan koy te jeg ɗelem jiig. Te layee, "Hee, fangooles fa ndeɓ fee! Tam ret o?" Fangool fa 
ndeɓ fee a jaahiɗ. Fangool a ref u! A jega o nand. Soxla'ee a naf, mbaa a kand, mbaa a caf. 
Soxla'ee o yet mbaa te weƴ kom faaɓ. A jega fop. Fangooloo.

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the 
title "letters", "syllables" and "individual 
score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils 
find the decodable story for this lesson. 
Instruct pupils who are not being assessed to 
read the story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: O maad ahe dama o tew . I niir pur i and har xewu.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they 
should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 

Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of 
the list.

activities.title: Comprehension – Comprehension questions

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending". 

Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:

book. Read the first word.

• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building

Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.

the board.
·    Say:  O ñuxuree refu "dami". Ndiiki, i njega yo o ñuxuree fop. I niirandoorin. (Pupils read 
the word)
·    Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with 
the rest of the words.
Words: daba dami dibi   
Use syllables to build new words
·    Say:  Ndiiki, bugaam nu njeem nu njagand xa ñuxur!
·    Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they 
know and write it in their copy books.
·    Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share 
the word they made.

Joon fa Mari
Kom leng, Joon teel'ee yokoox. Faap Joon, Baa Pool a layee, Joon, haƴa ret kiro jangik haye? 
Joon a dooninee, "I mbega yo a ƭatee." Joon a ƴuf a paax a rok kam pambe ke fu paal ke. Te a 
ñufand a xotik a kin ake. Mari o ndeɓ Joon o tewoo. Mari dimble a Joon koy de cooɗ ƥaaɓaan 
ke ñaamel.
Mari a cooɗ a cek ake puusiin. Joon a cooɗ pambe ke fu paal ke daaƭ. Ƥaaɓaan ke fop a lalit 
cawarte den. Mari sawar a. A layee, 'Ƥaaɓaan ke a sawar a yii yo a paax!' Mari laamit a Joon, 
a layinee, 'I cooɗ a ngee ƥaaɓaan ke ñaamel, har daaw keegu a den? Joon a layinee, "A ngon 
keegayii. In fop mbaru den o topatoox pur de ñoowoo. Ƥaaɓaan pind a ndefu. Joon a ɓaat o 
layee, "A ndef a ngaa ƥaaɓaan a koƥ kom ñiig fu njaf, han a mbaag o topatoox a qoox den. 
"Ndaa pambe in ke, paal ke fa a cek in ake in naa cooɗaa den ñaamel, foofi, fu kenand. Yaay 
Joon fa Mari a gar maaga. A layee, nu topatoox xa yo ƥaaɓaan ke a paax. A sawar a yo, ino 
tamit I sawara yo.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit 
with you.

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may 
indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning 
of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to 
say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that 
starts with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next 
letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have 
already learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to 
participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant 
and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say 
the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who 
flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most 
of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they 
are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more 
syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items 
aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other 
place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables 
they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of 
appreciation from the class.

the board.
• Say: O ñuxuree refu "fabi". Ndiiki, i mbinda yo o ñuxuree fop. I niirandoorin.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with

• Words: fabi, femi, bafa

the word they made.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound.Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate 
as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say 
its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). 
Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the flashcards. When 
they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has 
raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a 
clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to 
say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. 
Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote

the board.

read the word)

syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with 
the rest of the words.

• Say:Ndiiki, njeem yo ƭeet ndax nu mbaaga njagand xa ñuxur a qoox nuun! Ndiiki, bugaam 
nu njagandood xa ñuxur.

activities.title: Letter and keyword

sound.

nanel ake koy nu mbookatir a en /k aa f/ "kaaf"

sound, and then the syllable.

syllables independently again from their books..

column.

to read the word.

try the same word by themselves.

ake na safe cangir nuun. Nu jaf feraand le, niir yo hiɓ le koy nu lay o ñuxuree. Njoox yo qol 
nuun ndeef.

O Qooxoox ohe fo o Faamee
Meen a reeɗ'u reeɗ, o qooxoox o leng gen'u Baara.
Komookom, a naanga yii  jalaa a paax no qolum.
A duuf'a a qaƥ. A qaƥ ake a sax a paax. 
O qooxoox ohe a faax a yii.
O huu refna a ciyaaŋ a qaƥ.
A ciya o maad ohe fa yaayum.
Kom leng, o maad ohe a layee, "Ati a qaƥ pur kom xumbel le." 
O qooxoox ohe a ret no qolum.
Ye te retaa, ten het fu o faamee.
O faamee a layinee, "Feedeejam, o qooxoox ohe!"
O qooxoox ohe a dooninee, "Feedeejam, o camines!"
O faamee a layinee, "Dimle aam in raxin njaf ne. Ahe ñaama daaƭ le fop." 
O qooxoox ohe a layee, "O jaɓangaa in ŋaayong han tamitoŋ."
O faamee a heb o qooxoox ohe de ndaxin njaf ne. 
Ndaa njaf ne a ƴufee ga yii a paax.
Mbaag i ran  o ndam.
Koy o qooxoox ohe a jang gidi um fee. Paa! Njaf ne a diid koy te ƴuf koƭu.
O faamee a layee, "Han damito ŋ o ɓis a qaƥ ake men o maad ohe." 
Nu mbine no maad ohe, deno fop sawar'u yo.
O maad ohe a layee, "O faamee, jookanjal! He ɗaaxoŋ o gen fa in." 
Koy o faamee a gen fa den a damitaa wiin we fop

activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story

pupils.

• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.

should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit 
with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may 
indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning 
of the list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils found 
challenging in the assessment. The skill reinforced by the 
activity is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or "syllable 
blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have learnt 
but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the letter 
sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils 
to think of a word that starts with the sound. Calls 
on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on 
to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate 
as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant 
and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say 
the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who 
flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most 
of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are 
correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables 
for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. 
Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote 
down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation 
from the class.

picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the

Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.

the board.
• Say: : O ñuxuree refu "keebaa". Ndiiki, I mbinda yo o ñuxuree fop. I niirandoorin. (Pupils 
read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with 
the rest of the words.
 Words: keebaa, …./kadi/… maama,/…. faama, …/kama 
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Ndiiki, bugaam nu njeem bo nga' ndax han nu mbaag o leem xa ñuxur. 
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they 
know and write it in their copy books.

 the word they made.

Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)

De ƈuf, a ƈuf, a ƈuf.
Palak ke rek, de mbad na ngas. 
Foofi o ndik reeɗ'u na ngasee.
Fambe le a layee, "Ndiiki han i njeng foofi laa i yer na."
O ɓoxakoƥee a jaɓ a layee, "Iyo han i njeng foofi laa i yer na." 
O ɓoxakoƥee a fool kam a ngasee.
Fambe le tamit a fool kam a ngasee.
O ɓoxakoƥee a yer foofi, a yer, a yer, a yer. 
Fambe le a yer foofi, a yer, a yer, a yer.
De yeroo mbaa a ngeƴoo. Yede mbarna o sutoox.
O ɓoxakoƥee a layee, "A ngasee a hooɗa yii, waagiim o sutoox."
Fambe le a jaɓ a layee, "Iyo, a ngasee a hooɗa yii. Waagiim o sutoox! Ndiiki har i mbi'kaa?

O toog ohe a damit fambe le a sutin kam a ngasee.
Fambe le a gidim o toog o teɓ ohe koy a bug o ret. Nu ñufu, te ga' o ɓoxakoƥee kam mbog.

Fambe le a dooninee, "Iyo, han damtong. Ndaa fok o jang ne waroo na o damit a 
xaariitof."

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check predictions based on title
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupil predicted before the read aloud. Ask the pupils 
if his prediction matched what was in the story.
• Ask the other pupils to think about what they predicted. Call on 2 pupils at random. Ask   
 what they predicted, why, and if what they predicted is what happened in the story. 
5. Vocabulary - after reading (5 mins)
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their 
own words.
• Say: I njang xa ñuxur ake i njang iina pur i njagand xa ƭelem a qas.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - a sentence that is not in 
the pupil book or read aloud.
• For each of the other vocabulary words introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the 
word in a new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or 
correct the pupils, depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. Encourage 
pupils to share the words with their families at home.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "…l…" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Keek refu o hiiƈ in o xasee nu kom ne. O hiiƈeek o nanelum refu /l/. I layandoorin /l/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the small letter "l" on the alphabet poster or on the board again. 
• Say: Ke moƴna o may i naangaan o nga'taa neek kam xa ñuxur.

Keyword picture study
• Say: Har nu nga'u?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the 
sound.
• Say: I layandoor o ñuxuree "ligid". Ndax nu mbaaga o nan /l/ kam "ligid"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: O ñuxuree refu "ligid".
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part 
of the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of 
the syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "l" and show the "i". 
• Say: Har refu o nanelee?(pupils respond "i")
• Cover the "i" and show the "l".
• Say: Har refu o nanelee?(pupils respond l").
• Say: Nu mbaaga mbokatir xa nanel ake koy nu niir o hiɓ le. Ndiiki, niir yo xa nanel ake nu 
yooɓu /l/ /i/ "li".
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the  
 syllables independently again from their books. 
• Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each 
column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to 
it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say:Nangiloox yo a paax koy nu ƭeet. Han niir o hiɓ koy fokatirin jeg o ñuxur.

• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together 
to read the word.
• Say: I njeemin ƭeet.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to 
try the same word by themselves.
• Say: Ndiiki nu anda ke nu mbar na o mbi'. Kom ne nu mbi'teeguuna, niir yo a pind a lakas 
ake na safe cangir nuun. Nu jaf feraand le, niir yo hiɓ le koy nu lay o ñuxuree. Njoox yo qol 
koy nu ndeef.
• (Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading  
 the syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

activities.title: Assessment: BEFORE THE LESSON
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the 
title "letters", "syllables" and "individual 
score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils 
find the decodable story for this lesson. 
Instruct pupils who are not being assessed to 
read the story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Xa ƥiy xa koor a ƭak fu o ƥiy o ndew awe took o sar. Fat i niir pur and har a mbiyaa. 
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they   
 should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit 
with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may 
indicate that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A 
total of 40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider 
reinforcement activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning 
of the list.

the assessment. The skill reinforced by 
the activity is in the activity name: "letter 
sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to 
say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that 
starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the 
next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have 
already learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to 
participate as possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards 
(try to use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant 
and say its sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say 
the sound). Ask pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the two 
flashcards. When they agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until 
most of the class has raised their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If 
they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 
more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 

Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items   
 aloud once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or   
 other place. Call one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the   
 syllables they wrote down raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get  
 a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the 
pupil book. Read the first word.
• Say: Har refu o ñuxureek? kaaf? 
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the 
picture on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in 
the list and whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word 
for the class. Ask all pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.Continue the 
activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Mexe xelaataa o ñuxur. O ñuxuree refu "laalo". I xaaj o ñuxuree koy mbox xa qiɓ 
ake: /laa/ /lo/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil 
Books. Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written 
on the board.
• Say: O ñuxuree refu "laalo". Ndiiki, i mbind a yo o ñuxuree fop. I niirandoorin.
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word 
in their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue 
with the rest of the words.
 Words: /laalo/ /maalo/ /foofi/ /kaala/
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Ndiiki, bugaam nu njeem bo ga' ndax han nu mbaag o njagand xa ñuxur.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they 
know and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to 
share the word they made.
